title: Call and Thank Senator Yundt for Standing Up for Public Education
description:
# Thank Senator Yundt for Standing Up for Public Education

**Senator Robert Yundt** played a pivotal role in bringing *HB 57*, the bipartisan education bill, to the floor of the Alaska Senate. He helped broker agreements between the Senate Majority and Minority caucuses — and when it counted most, he voted to **override Governor Dunleavy’s veto**.

He was the **only Senator from the Mat-Su** to vote for the override.

Senator Yundt’s leadership helped protect funding for Alaska’s students, educators, and schools. But we know the fight isn’t over — if the governor tries to use **line-item vetoes** to gut education funding, we’ll need Senator Yundt’s support again.

**Let’s thank him — and remind him we’re counting on his continued leadership.**
If you would rather email him (not as effective) here is his email address: **Email:** [Senator.Robert.Yundt@akleg.gov](mailto:Senator.Robert.Yundt@akleg.gov)

---

Here is a draft script to modify.

> Hello, my name is \_\_\_\_\_\_ and I live in \_\_\_\_\_\_.  
>  
> I’m calling to **thank Senator Yundt** for his leadership on HB 57 and for voting to override Governor Dunleavy’s veto. I truly appreciate that he was willing to work across the aisle and stand up for our public schools — and that he was the only Senator from the Mat-Su to do so.  
>  
> I hope Senator Yundt will continue to support education by **overriding any future line-item vetoes** that would reduce funding for Alaska’s schools.  
>  
> Please let him know that his leadership made a real difference and that his constituents are paying attention.  
>  
> Thank you.

title: Virtual Florida State Budget Review w/Rep. Eskamani

title: Postcard Party in Lakeview!
description:
On June 10th at 6 PM, we'll be coming together to save democracy by writing postcards to voters in Virginia to get out the vote in the November election. We will provide the postcards, the addresses, and the script.  You provide the stamps for the postcards you write or donate!  

Why write postcards to Virginia? 

Voters in Virginia will head to the polls this November to pick a new governor. Former Rep. Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, and Virginia Lt. Gov. Winsome Earle-Sears, a MAGA Republican, are the candidates.

This is a state race, but one with national implications.
(1)The Commonwealth is a national bellwether. It is here where positions, comms, and policy can, and will, be tested and impact the 2026 midterms. 
 (2) Held in the odd year after the presidential election since 1869, Virginia’s gubernatorial race is a cyclical scorecard for voters’ moods and the issues at the forefront of the national consciousness. This enables learning and adjustments for '26   
(3)  A Spanberger win will lessen the MAGA hold on Governorships, which is crucial to change MAGA policies at the state level 
(4) A Republican win in Virginia might be seen as a major embrace of Trump and Trumpism, even if it gets decided on other grounds. 
(5) Down-ballot races matter. While the governor’s race is always the marquee race, Virginia will also be electing all 100 members of the House of Delegates, where Democrats hold the narrowest of margins, 51-49.

So, come join us at Beermiscuous to write postcards to VA voters. Remember to bring postcard stamps!.

Let's do this!

title: Tues. 5/27 > I-91 Overpass Standout - 9 Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

title: D-Day Rally ~ No Suckers or Losers, Only Heroes
description:
Honor Our Heroes - D-Day Remembrance & Veterans Protest Rally

Join us as we gather in remembrance of one of the most pivotal days in our history—D-Day, June 6, 1944—to honor the courage and sacrifice of the American heroes who stormed the beaches of Normandy and fought for freedom around the world.

But this year, we do more than remember—we raise our voices in protest.

There are no suckers. No losers. Only heroes.

We stand in unity against any rhetoric or policy that disrespects or undermines the value of our veterans. Recent and ongoing cuts to the Veterans Administration by the current administration are a betrayal of those who have risked their lives for our country. These cuts threaten access to essential healthcare, support services, and dignity for the very people who defended our freedoms.

Make your message heard!

Bring signs that honor the sacrifices of our veterans and speak out against the disrespect and defunding of those who served. We encourage messages that include:

“No Cuts, Just Care”
“Honor All Who Served”
“D-Day Heroes Deserve More”
“Veterans Are Not Political Pawns”
“There Are No Suckers or Losers—Only Heroes”

Let’s turn our collective outrage into action—respectfully, powerfully, and visibly.

Let’s show our local veterans and their families that we see them, we honor them, and we will fight for them just as they once fought for us.

Stand for our heroes. Stand against injustice. See you there.

#FightingforDemocracy #SupportOurVeterans

description:
